checks.issue: ‼‼ เคลัญเญนาภิปีพิโต — A FOURTH BARE ?/พ, AND THIS ONE CUTS AGAINST WHAT PAGES 76-80 SEEMED TO ESTABLISH. Standard Pali is gelaññenābhipīḷito, 'afflicted by illness', with ฬ; abhipībito is not a word. The letter is BARE and at 7x stacked directly above the พ of อาพาธา two rows below it on this same sheet it is identical — two humps, no ascender. THE PROBLEM: pages 76, 77, 78 and 80 each showed a bare ฬ carrying an OBVIOUS tall ascender (จักกะวาเฬสุ, อัฏฐะจัตตาฬีสะ), which is why 'a bare ฬ can be read from the photograph' was written down as a rule. This page shows a bare position where the canon demands ฬ and there is no ascender at all. So EITHER this printer sets some bare ฬ without an ascender — and the rule is wrong — OR the book really does print พ in all four places. Reproduced as printed. This is now FOUR instances: pages 85, 90, 95 and 97.

TWO COLUMNS, gutter measured at x 900-1020 — a different position from the บทขัด above it on this sheet, whose gutter is at x 860-1020. Each profiled separately. Read ACROSS. FIRST PAIRING FOR CHECKING: left โพชฌังโค สะติสังขาโต + right ธัมมานัง วิจะโย ตะถา.

เอเตนะ สัจจะวัชเชนะ โสตถิ เต โหตุ สัพพะทา. CLOSES ALL FOUR STANZAS — verses 6, 10, 14 and 17 — word for word. Recorded because check_render walks strings in printed order and four verbatim repeats on one sheet is exactly the shape that reads as a fault.

ติณณันนัมปิ มะเหสินัง — 'of all three great Seekers'. The three are Moggallāna and Kassapa from verse 7 and the Buddha himself from verse 11, which is what makes the last stanza the conclusion of the other three rather than a fourth story. The English says so plainly because the Pali only implies it.

A COLOPHON AND NO CITATION. โพชฌังคะปะริตตัง นิฏฐิตัง. is printed centred under verse 17 and goes in as `closing`. No footnote and no marker anywhere on the sheet, so source_printed is left off — the same as the Mora, Vaṭṭaka and Aṅgulimāla parittas.

batch_status.notes: ‼‼ THE ฬ/พ QUESTION TOOK A TURN ON THIS PAGE AND MY EARLIER CONCLUSION NEEDS REVISING. Verse 11 prints เคลัญเญนาภิปีพิโต with a BARE พ — identical at 7x to the พ of อาพาธา two rows below — where standard Pali is gelaññenābhipīḷito with ฬ. That is the FOURTH instance, after pages 85, 90 and 95. THE POINT: pages 76 to 80 each showed a bare ฬ carrying an obvious tall ascender, which is why 'a bare ฬ can be read from the photograph' was written into the brief as a rule. This page shows a bare position where the canon demands ฬ and there is NO ascender. So either the printer sets some bare ฬ without one — and that rule is wrong — or the book really prints พ in all four places. Both readings are still consistent with everything seen; the photographs cannot choose between them. FOUR WORDS NOW WAIT ON ONE LOOK AT THE BOOK. diacritic_exceptions: satta/sattā — genuinely two different words, and the BOOK prints the difference. The preface's verse 3 reads เยปิเม สัตตา with the long า — sattā, 'beings', the subject of the sentence. The paritta's verse 8 reads โพชฌังเค สัตตะ เทสะยิ with the short ะ — satta, 'seven', counting the factors. Long against short is visible on the page and the two are unrelated words; making them agree would turn 'he taught the seven factors' into 'he taught beings factors'.
